unassigned_checked.why: The list of unassigned episodes, required reading. No entry is titled as an update or continuation of a Season 15 story (the Diana updates are inside s15_08).
Opened because Lex Fitzgerald's story (E8-E9) is cyber-stalking and this episode might discuss it. It is a general statistics episode and mentions no Season 15 person.

persons.name: Holly
persons.harm: Moved into the Playboy Mansion as one of the founder's girlfriends; on her first night, drunk, she was pushed into group sex with him, then lived for about seven years under his control (curfew, not allowed to work, triangulation, security following her) and verbal/emotional abuse.

quotes.quote: If somebody were to tell [perpetrator] something about you that he didn't like and all your stuff would be packed up and I'd have nowhere to go.
And I realized it dawned on me that he had been the problem the whole time.

persons.outcome_quote: I left, and it was emotionally harrowing for me because I did feel very, very guilty.
persons.notes: No institution was told about the abuse; the story never discusses reporting, so the reasons listed are the reasons she gives for staying silent and staying (fear of being kicked out with nowhere to live; not seeing him as the problem until later). She asked the founder's secretary's office about pay and screen credits for the TV show (@44:39-45:42) and got them, but that was about pay, not the abuse, so it is not coded as a contact. She briefly mentions going straight into another controlling relationship afterwards (@61:08, security following her). That is a one-line mention with no further story, so it has no record of its own. Family knew nothing (@24:58-25:58).

persons.name: Valentina
persons.harm: In her senior year a stranger strangled her unconscious in an alley near her off-campus house, threatened her with a knife and sexually assaulted her. He was later identified as a serial rapist.

contacts.when: the night of the attack, senior year (October)
contacts.what_was_asked: Help after being strangled and sexually assaulted in an alley.
contacts.what_institution_did: The responding officer questioned her, then at the hospital went through her friend's phone and asked whether she 'does this a lot'.
contacts.quote: One thing that was sort of odd was when she came in that police officer that had come to talk to me initially he stopped her and asked to see her phone and look through her text and saw that I texted her that I was attacked and he said does she do this a lot.
contacts.what_happened_next: The same officer got angry with her father and said she was hiding things (@13:26).
contacts.notes: Also: 'the officer ended up getting mad at my dad and saying that I wasn't being forthright with my information and that I was hiding things' (@13:26).

contacts.what_was_asked: Medical care and a rape kit.
contacts.what_institution_did: Took her to hospital by ambulance, where a rape kit was done.
contacts.quote: he didn't want to be around me in the hospital when I was getting things like the rape kit done
contacts.what_happened_next: She went home with her parents. A concussion was found later.
contacts.notes: Little detail is given about the hospital's response.

contacts.institution: police detective (first detective on the case)
contacts.what_was_asked: Investigation, find the attacker.
contacts.what_institution_did: The detective investigated and told her he believed something happened to her; he was then taken off the case.
contacts.quote: I ended up talking to a specific detective during most of that initially and he ended up saying to me at one point I believe something happened to you which was sort of amazing for me to hear because I did feel like I was being told that I drank too much and I didn't know what I was essentially talking about.
contacts.what_happened_next: He was replaced by the officer who first responded. The case was never solved.

contacts.what_was_asked: Investigation.
contacts.what_institution_did: Officers treated her and her family as if they were hiding things, and gave a false account of the man she had been with.
contacts.quote: So a lot of it was strange, especially how the officers acted towards me and my family at that time, they acted like I was hiding things that everyone was hiding things.
contacts.what_happened_next: She felt 'like I was the one who was in the wrong' (@15:32-16:32).
contacts.notes: The officers said the man she had been with was not cooperating, which he denied (@14:27).

contacts.what_was_asked: To finish coursework from home after the attack.
contacts.what_institution_did: Most professors accommodated her; one psychology professor suggested she take the semester off.
contacts.quote: most of the teachers that I reached out to about doing homework and things like that and getting information at home because of what happened were very, very willing to work with me except for one of my psychology professors was like, you should think about taking this semester off.
contacts.what_happened_next: She graduated on time.
contacts.notes: One professor suggested she take the semester off.

contacts.what_was_asked: Her father wrote to complain about how the case was being handled.
contacts.what_institution_did: The president had not known and expressed sympathy; no step is shown.
contacts.quote: It was technically off campus, so my dad, he ended up writing a letter to the president because he was so frustrated. The president didn't know anything about this and it was like, I'm so sorry this happened.
contacts.what_happened_next: Nothing further is described.

contacts.what_was_asked: Help and guidance.
contacts.what_institution_did: Told her she had already done everything right; no further help is described.
contacts.quote: There was an advocate center that someone referred me to and I walked there and they told me that I was doing everything right basically and that I had already done everything they would have told me to do. It wasn't as helpful as I would have hoped
contacts.what_happened_next: Nothing further is described.

contacts.institution: police (replacement detective, the original responding officer)
contacts.when: after the first detective was moved
contacts.what_was_asked: Continued investigation.
contacts.what_institution_did: The new detective was the officer who first responded; he got defensive when she asked about the first detective.
contacts.quote: That detective ended up being switched out. The new detective was the police officer that had initially responded to my case.
contacts.what_happened_next: He was 'very defensive and not pleasant to work with' (@18:36). The case was not solved.
contacts.notes: The quote shows the switch and his defensiveness; it does not show what he did on the case.

contacts.what_was_asked: Therapy.
contacts.what_institution_did: She saw a therapist; nothing more is described.
contacts.quote: I had been seeing a therapist right after that happened and I thought I felt better
contacts.what_happened_next: Years later she found a therapist who helped (@26:54).

contacts.when: years later, after news that a serial rapist had been arrested
contacts.what_was_asked: Asked whether the arrested man had been considered for her case.
contacts.what_institution_did: Said she had been the first case they thought of, but no one had contacted her.
contacts.quote: Did you guys think about him possibly being the person that attacked me and they were still sort of strange about it? And like, oh, yeah, you're of the top one we thought of when all this came down and I was just like, I don't understand why no one called B or anything like that, but okay.
contacts.what_happened_next: She was not told about his court date.

contacts.institution: prosecution and court in the serial rapist's case
contacts.what_was_asked: (institution acted on its own)
contacts.what_institution_did: He was convicted for other attacks and admitted hers in a statement; she was called and told he had admitted it; he got 40 years. Her attack was not charged.
contacts.quote: He admitted to having attacked these women and they got his statement about other women that he wasn't charged for and one of them ended up being me, which it was crazy because that was the first time that someone had called me and been like, hey, so he admitted to what he did to you and we're so, so sorry this happened.
contacts.what_happened_next: He is in prison for 40 years and she gets updates on where he is (@25:52, @26:54).
contacts.notes: Coded acted_partly because her attack was never charged and she was not told about his court date. His conviction and imprisonment do protect others from him.

persons.outcome_quote: He ended up getting 40 years in prison.
persons.decisive_work_quote: They had tested his DNA and realized that he was connected to all these rapes and attacks from the college that I attended.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: years later, after she had graduated and started working (DNA match after another victim identified him)
persons.notes: harmed_by_institution_ever is true because police treated her as if she were lying or to blame ('It was like I was the one who was in the wrong', @15:32). Outcome is coded protected because the harm was a single attack that had ended, and institutional action removed the attacker (40 years). But he was never charged for her attack, and he was caught through another victim's case. Evidence: conviction for other victims plus his admission of her attack. No document was read on air. She says it 'could have been prevented had the police taken stuff more seriously' (@19:37-20:37).

persons.name: [unnamed] victim who knew the serial rapist (friend of his girlfriend)
persons.harm: Sexually assaulted by the same serial rapist; she woke to him breathing heavily and knew who he was.

contacts.what_was_asked: Report and rape kit.
contacts.what_institution_did: Collected a rape kit; DNA tied him to the earlier attacks; he was arrested and convicted.
contacts.quote: He had finally attacked someone that knew who he was, which is how he was discovered.
contacts.what_happened_next: He admitted the attacks and got 40 years (@24:49-25:52).

persons.outcome_quote: He ended up getting 40 years in prison.

persons.name: Naomi
persons.harm: Over about two years a therapist coworker she considered her best friend told her a long string of fake tragedies and medical emergencies (staged accident, fake cancer), turned her against other friends with lies, forcibly kissed her at dinner, and told lies about her and colleagues.

quotes.quote: I was like, I don't know if I can do that. Everybody loves her. What if they don't believe me?
I think at this point in time I was a bit in survival mode of I need to go to work and keep my job and I need to keep the peace.

contacts.institution: the therapeutic agency (its owner, her boss)
contacts.when: a few days after the coworker's staged 'major car accident', about two years into the friendship
contacts.what_was_asked: To look into whether the accident really happened.
contacts.what_institution_did: At first put her doubts down to the coworker's concussion; agreed to look into it; three weeks later told her the accident had happened.
contacts.quote: And he's like, hey, it happened. I was like, what? And he's like, everything happened. She got in the accident, it happened.
contacts.what_happened_next: The owner paid the coworker's wages for about two months and made a back-to-work plan (@4:11). Naomi felt guilty and 'doubled down on our friendship'.
contacts.notes: His first reply was 'oh, I'm sure with her concussion, the details are foggy' (s15-ep3 @54:17). He did agree to look into it, so acted_partly also fits. Disbelieved was chosen because the quote shows him rejecting her concern.

contacts.when: months later, after the coworker claimed a cancer diagnosis with chemo that Friday
contacts.what_was_asked: She told him the coworker was lying and dangerous.
contacts.what_institution_did: Told her at first to 'chill on accusations'; after she explained how cancer treatment works, he took her seriously, asked knowledgeable friends, and looked for an HR person to learn his rights.
contacts.quote: After I explained the whole cancer thing, he started taking me seriously. He was like, okay, let me look into it.
contacts.what_happened_next: He came back saying 'it is maybe not true' and consulted HR (@15:31-16:38).
contacts.notes: Initially: 'chill on accusations. She's going through a lot of motions or heightened' (@9:25).

contacts.institution: the therapeutic agency (owner, with an HR lawyer)
contacts.what_was_asked: (employer acting on the information)
contacts.what_institution_did: Took advice from an HR lawyer and stopped her using company time for her appointments, putting pressure on her attendance.
contacts.quote: He consulted with an HR lawyer and they were like, okay, you have the right to not allow an employee to leave work for XYZ amounts of hours for their appointments and she had exceeded that.
contacts.what_happened_next: With 'the walls ... closing in', the coworker checked herself into a mental health facility, where she could not be fired, admitted the lies and quit (@27:03-28:04, @43:36).
contacts.notes: The employer could not fire her while she was in the facility.

persons.outcome_quote: She was in a mental health facility and she she understood Blabberlaw, and she knew that she could not be fired. So she quit while she was there.
persons.decisive_work_quote: You have somebody so dangerous working in your agency. You need to fucking pay attention seriously.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: about six months after she first raised it with her boss (after the cancer claim)
persons.notes: The never_reached reasons are about the forced kiss (s15-ep3 @36:13), which she never reported. 'Other' = job security ('she's way smarter than me ... If I blow this up ... I won't have a job', @41:31). Outcome is partly_protected because the deception at work ended when the coworker quit under employer pressure; she was never removed, and nothing was done about the forced kiss or the lies. Naomi did decisive work beyond reporting: she pressed her boss again, checked stories with Alice, and called the coworker's mother, who confirmed the stories were false (s15-e4 @29:10-33:26). John and Alice corroborate the pattern as second witnesses. A couple of colleagues tried to report her to the licensing body (coded under Alice).

persons.name: Alice
persons.harm: The same coworker was her roommate: she drank and replaced her alcohol, ate her things, hid drug use, played mind games with hidden bottles, and told others lies about her (that she grew up in a cult, that her father had died), cutting her off from Naomi.

contacts.when: while the roommate still lived with her
contacts.what_was_asked: Guidance on handling the roommate.
contacts.what_institution_did: Helped her set limits.
contacts.quote: I was also getting guidance from my own therapist at this time and learning how to navigate this and set limits and also show compassion and empathy.
contacts.what_happened_next: She asked the roommate to leave, and the roommate moved out the next month.

contacts.institution: licensing body where the coworker was licensed
contacts.what_was_asked: To report the coworker's conduct.
contacts.what_institution_did: Would not take the report because they were not her clients.
contacts.quote: A couple of us tried to make a report where our license is based. It's complicated, but basically we were given the feedback that we couldn't because we weren't clients.
contacts.what_happened_next: 'That sucked. I felt helpless.' No further action.
contacts.notes: The speaker of this passage is not clearly identified (it may be John). It says 'a couple of us', so it is placed here and mentioned under Naomi.

persons.outcome_quote: There's been no contact since then.
persons.notes: The harm in the shared flat ended when Alice asked the roommate to leave, not through any institution. The licensing body would not take a report.

persons.name: Diana
persons.harm: Her second husband, a retired police officer and veteran who lied about his war injuries, groomed her as a single mother and then sexually abused her niece and her daughter in their home. He shared images of the children in an online group and planned to trade them for abuse.

contacts.what_was_asked: (institution acted on its own, through an undercover agent in an online group)
contacts.what_institution_did: Arrested the husband for child sexual exploitation and producing child sexual abuse material, searched the home and seized devices.
contacts.quote: He informed me that they had been watching my husband for a period of time and that he has been arrested for sexual exploitation of a minor and production and manufacturing of sexual exploitation pornography.
contacts.what_happened_next: The children were interviewed at a child advocacy center the next day.

contacts.institution: the children's high school and elementary school (principals and counselors)
contacts.when: after news coverage led to bullying
contacts.what_was_asked: To stop bullying and talk about the case at school, and to support the children.
contacts.what_institution_did: Supported the children and made school safe for them.
contacts.quote: I wanted to make sure that I had the support of the school behind me, and they were very supportive and making sure that the kids felt safe and that this was a space that they could go to and get away from it.
contacts.what_happened_next: The children went back to school and their activities.

contacts.when: from after the arrest, weekly for 1.5+ years
contacts.what_was_asked: Trauma therapy for her and her daughters.
contacts.what_institution_did: Gave ongoing trauma therapy; when Gracie disclosed, advised Diana to ask Gracie whether she wanted to file a complaint.
contacts.quote: I had contacted my trauma therapist who has become a very dear friend now. And I said, what do I do? And she said, you need to have a conversation with Gracie as to whether or not she wants to move forward with this and file a complaint.
contacts.what_happened_next: Therapy continues (W2 @19:46).

contacts.what_was_asked: (prosecution kept her informed)
contacts.what_institution_did: Explained the sentencing factors, including his police and military background.
contacts.quote: I spoke with the prosecuting district attorney and she informed me that even the smallest of things such as his former employment of being a police officer and being in the military, those are things that they take into account the depth of the lies, how he hid the things that he had done and the danger that he would be to society if he got out.
contacts.what_happened_next: At sentencing the prosecutor read the children's statements and asked for a higher standard (W2 @5:06-6:09).

contacts.what_was_asked: Help preparing her victim impact statement.
contacts.what_institution_did: Walked her through court, but made her remove words like 'monster' and told her not to address him or show expression.
contacts.quote: I had said in there a couple times that [perpetrator] is a monster and my victim impact advocate, she's like, you can't say that in court, the judge won't allow it.
contacts.what_happened_next: She felt 'put in this box' (W1 @15:29) but read her statement, and the judge listened.

contacts.institution: the local child advocacy center and organizations it referred her to
contacts.what_was_asked: Practical support.
contacts.what_institution_did: Connected her to organizations that replaced the beds and paid some bills.
contacts.quote: my local center was able to put me in touch with an organization who paid for the replacement of all of the beds where the children had been assaulted.
contacts.what_happened_next: Bills were paid while she took time off.

contacts.what_was_asked: (prosecution)
contacts.what_institution_did: Accepted his guilty plea to the major federal charge and sentenced him to the maximum 30 years with no parole; the judge read her statement and said he saw no remorse.
contacts.quote: And he was sentenced to the full 30 years, no chance of parole.
contacts.what_happened_next: Seven county (state) counts are still pending (W2 @10:17).

persons.outcome_quote: And he was sentenced to the full 30 years, no chance of parole.
persons.decisive_work_quote: Fortunately the person that he was talking to was an undercover FBI agent.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: immediate: the FBI acted first (undercover operation and arrest)
persons.notes: The harm to Diana (a marriage built on deception and grooming, and the exploitation of children in her care) was ended by the FBI arrest, which came before any report. Documents read on air: her victim impact statement, Gracie's statement, and excerpts from the court transcript (W2 @8:10). Second witness: the husband's military colleague on his lies (@36:24). Her sister (the niece's mother) died by suicide in October 2022 (W1 @27:51). In her statement Diana says she had 'just came out of an abusive marriage' (W1 @25:46); that is a one-line mention of a separate harm with no further story, so it has no record of its own. The husband's mother blamed her (@44:48), but she is not an institution.

coder_notes: All 8 chunk files were read in full to their stated last lines. Season 15 holds 13 numbered episodes plus two What Came Next updates on Diana (E5). E10-E11 update Season 9 (Danielle) and E13 updates Season 7 (Amy B. Chesler). Only events told in this season are coded for those people. E12 is an expert episode on consent law; the one case it narrates in full (the Purdue student) has a record, and public-case references are in others_mentioned. Coding conventions: (1) When a person told a therapist about the harm, that counts as the harm reaching a medical_or_therapy institution. (2) Perpetrators' names are replaced with [perpetrator] in every quotation; non-victim third parties are described by role, and quotes were chosen to avoid their names. (3) Speakers in E3/E4 are sometimes hard to tell apart. The licensing-body report ('A couple of us') is coded under Alice but may have been made by John. John (E3/E4) is a narrating colleague with no harm story of his own, so he has no record. Two one-line mentions of separate harms (Holly's next controlling boyfriend; Diana's earlier abusive marriage) are noted in those people's records rather than given records. Kenji (S9) has reached_institution 'unclear', because these episodes describe no institution for him. Many 'contacts' in Lex's story are false CPS reports made by her harassers, coded with initiated_by third_party.
